A children's rhyme says, "On bingchen, Dragon Tail hides in chen; in full mourning dress, splendidly arrayed, seize Guo's banner; Quail blazes bright; Celestial Lance gleams; Fire at culmination forms the army." Surely that means the junction of the ninth and tenth months! On bingzi at dawn the sun will be in Tail, the moon in Lance, and Quail Fire at culmination—that must be the moment. Lance enters Tail at twelve degrees. The new calendar places the fixed new moon of the tenth month on bingzi that year, with sun and moon conjoined at fourteen degrees of Tail on the ecliptic. The ancient calendar has the sun in Tail while the moon is in Lance; hence "Dragon Tail hides in chen." By ancient reckoning, at dawn Extended Net stands at culmination; Quail Fire is at its end and just beginning to descend westward; hence "blazes bright."
54
昭公七年四月甲辰朔，日蝕。 士文伯曰：「去衞地，如魯地。 於是有災，魯實受之。 」新曆是歲二月甲辰朔入常，雨水後七日，在奎十度。 周度為降婁之始，則魯、衞之交也。 自周初至是已退七度，故入雨水。 七日方及降婁，雖日度潛移，而周禮未改，其配神主祭之宿，宜書於建國之初。 淳風駁戊寅曆曰：「漢志降婁初在奎五度，今曆日蝕在降婁之中，依無歲差法，食於兩次之交。 」是又不然。 議者曉十有二次之所由生，然後可以明其得失。 且劉歆等所定辰次，非能有以覩陰陽之賾，而得於鬼神，各據當時中節星度耳。 歆以太初曆冬至日在牽牛前五度，故降婁直東壁八度。 李業興正光曆，冬至在牽牛前十二度，故降婁退至東壁三度。 及祖沖之後，以為日度漸差，則當據列宿四正之中，以定辰次，不復係於中節。 淳風以冬至常在斗十三度，則當以東壁二度為降婁之初，安得守漢曆以駁仁均耶？ 又三統曆昭公二十年，己丑，日南至，與麟德及開元曆同。 然則入雨水後七日，亦入降婁七度，非魯、衞之交也。 三十一年十二月辛亥朔，日蝕。 史墨曰：「日月在辰尾，庚午之日，日始有讁。 」開元曆是歲十月辛亥朔，入常立冬。 五日，日在尾十三度，於古距辰尾之初。 麟德曆日在心三度於黃道，退直于房矣。
In the seventh year of Duke Zhao, on the jiachen new moon of the fourth month, there was a solar eclipse. Shi Wenbo said, "Leaving Wei's territory, it is like Lu's territory." Accordingly there will be calamity, and Lu will in fact bear it. The new calendar places that year's second-month jiachen new moon in the constant cycle, seven days after Rain Water, at ten degrees of Straddler. In Zhou degrees this is the start of Descending Harvest—the border between Lu and Wei. From early Zhou to this point the sun had already retreated seven degrees; hence the eclipse falls in Rain Water. Only on the seventh day does it reach Descending Harvest; though solar degrees silently shift, Zhou ritual remains unchanged—the lodges paired with spirit tablets for sacrifice should be recorded as they were at the founding of the state. Chunfeng, refuting the Wuyin calendar, says, "The Han Treatise places the start of Descending Harvest at five degrees of Straddler; the present calendar's eclipse falls in the middle of Descending Harvest; by the method that ignores precession, the eclipse should fall at the junction of two stations." That too is incorrect. Those who debate these matters must first understand how the twelve stations arise; only then can they judge what is right and wrong. Moreover, the station assignments fixed by Liu Xin and others were not obtained by penetrating the depths of yin and yang or receiving revelation from spirits—they simply relied on the mid-term star degrees of their own day. Xin, using the Taichu calendar with the winter solstice five degrees before Ox Leader, therefore places Descending Harvest directly at eight degrees of Eastern Wall. In Li Yexing's Zhengguang calendar the winter solstice falls twelve degrees before Ox Leader, so Descending Harvest retreats to three degrees of Eastern Wall. After Zu Chongzhi, believing that solar degrees gradually shift, one should fix the station assignments by the four cardinal points among the lodges, no longer tying them to mid-term solar terms. Chunfeng, with the winter solstice constantly at thirteen degrees of Dipper, should take two degrees of Eastern Wall as the start of Descending Harvest—how can he cling to the Han calendar to refute Ren Jun? Moreover, the Triple Concordance calendar for the twentieth year of Duke Zhao, jichou, places the winter solstice in agreement with the Linde and Kaiyuan calendars. Seven days after Rain Water also falls seven degrees into Descending Harvest—it is not the border of Lu and Wei. In the thirty-first year, on the xinhai new moon of the twelfth month, there was a solar eclipse. Shi Mo said, "Sun and moon are at Dragon Tail; on gengwu day the sun first shows a blemish." The Kaiyuan calendar places that year's tenth-month xinhai new moon in the constant cycle at Establishment of Winter. On the fifth day the sun stands at thirteen degrees of Tail—in ancient reckoning, at the start of Dragon Tail. The Linde calendar places the sun at three degrees of Heart on the ecliptic, retreated so that it aligns directly with Room.
55
哀公十二年冬十有二月，螽。 開元曆推置閏當在十一年春，至十二年冬，失閏已久。 是歲九月己亥朔，先寒露三日，於定氣，日在亢五度，去心近一次。 火星明大，尚未當伏。 至霜降五日，始潛日下。 乃月令「蟄蟲咸俯」，則火辰未伏，當在霜降前。 雖節氣極晚，不得十月昏見。 故仲尼曰：「丘聞之，火伏而後蟄者畢。 今火猶西流，司曆過也。 」方夏后氏之初，八月辰伏，九月內火，及霜降之後，火已朝覿東方，距春秋之季千五百餘年，乃云「火伏而後蟄者畢」。 向使冬至常居其所，則仲尼不得以西流未伏，明是九月之初也。 自春秋至今又千五百歲，麟德曆以霜降後五日，日在氐八度，房、心初伏，定增二日，以月蝕衝校之，猶差三度。 閏餘稍多，則建亥之始，火猶見西方。 向使宿度不移，則仲尼不得以西流未伏，明非十月之候也。 自羲、和已來，火辰見伏，三覩厥變。 然則丘明之記，欲令後之作者參求微象，以探仲尼之旨。 是歲失閏寖久，季秋中氣後天三日，比及明年仲冬，又得一閏。 寤仲尼之言，補正時曆，而十二月猶可以螽。 至哀公十四年五月庚申朔，日蝕。 以開元曆考之，則日蝕前又增一閏，魯曆正矣。 長曆自哀公十年六月，迄十四年二月，纔置一閏，非是。
In the twelfth year of Duke Ai, in the twelfth month of winter, there were locusts. The Kaiyuan calendar calculates that an intercalary month should have been inserted in the spring of the eleventh year; by the winter of the twelfth year the missed intercalation had long persisted. That year the ninth-month jihai new moon fell three days before Cold Dew; by fixed qi the sun stood at five degrees of Neck, one station short of Heart. Mars was bright and large, and had not yet reached its setting. Only on the fifth day after Frost Descent did it first hide beneath the sun. Yet the Monthly Ordinances says, "All hibernating creatures bow down"—which means Mars should have set before Frost Descent. Even if the solar term were extremely late, Mars could not still appear at dusk in the tenth month. Confucius therefore said, "I have heard that only after Fire sets are all the hibernating creatures finished." Yet Fire still moves westward—the calendar officers have erred. At the start of the Xia dynasty, the chen star set in the eighth month and Fire entered in the ninth; by after Frost Descent Fire had already appeared in the east at dawn—more than 1,500 years before the end of Spring and Autumn, and yet the text says, "Only after Fire sets are the hibernators finished." If the winter solstice always stayed in its place, Confucius could not have used Mars' westward motion and failure to set to show that it was the start of the ninth month. From Spring and Autumn to the present is another 1,500 years; the Linde calendar, five days after Frost Descent, places the sun at eight degrees of Root with Room and Heart just setting—adding two fixed days and checking against lunar eclipse opposition, it still differs by three degrees. If the intercalary surplus is slightly too large, at the start of Establishment of Boar Fire still appears in the west. If lodge degrees did not shift, Confucius could not have used Mars' westward motion and failure to set to show that it was not the sign of the tenth month. Since the time of Xi and He, Mars' appearances and settings have changed three times. Qiu Ming's record, then, is meant to lead later writers to compare subtle celestial signs and probe Confucius' meaning. That year the missed intercalation had long persisted; late autumn's mid-term qi lagged heaven by three days; by the next year's mid-winter another intercalary month could be inserted. Once one heeds Confucius' words and corrects the calendar, locusts in the twelfth month become intelligible. By the fourteenth year of Duke Ai, on the gengshen new moon of the fifth month, there was a solar eclipse. Examined with the Kaiyuan calendar, one more intercalary month is added before the eclipse, and Lu's calendar is corrected. The Long Calendar inserts only one intercalary month from the sixth month of Duke Ai's tenth year to the second month of his fourteenth year—that is incorrect.
56
戰國及秦，日却退三度。 始皇十七年辛未歲冬至，應在斗二十二度。 秦曆上元正月己巳朔，晨初立春，日、月、五星俱起營室五度，蔀首日名皆直四孟。 假朔退十五日，則閏在正月前。 朔進十五日，則閏在正月後。 是以十有二節，皆在盈縮之中，而晨昏宿度隨之。 以顓頊曆依月令自十有二節推之，與不韋所記合。 而潁子嚴之倫謂月令晨昏距宿，當在中氣，致雩祭太晚，自乖左氏之文，而杜預又據春秋以月令為否。 皆非是。 梁大同曆夏后氏之初，冬至日在牽牛初，以為明堂、月令乃夏時之記，據中氣推之不合，更以中節之間為正，迺稍相符。 不知進在節初，自然契合。 自秦初及今，又且千歲，節初之宿，皆當中氣。 淳風因為說曰：「今孟春中氣，日在營室，昏明中星，與月令不殊。 」按秦曆立春，日在營室五度。 麟德曆以啟蟄之日迺至營室，其昏明中宿十有二建，以為不差，妄矣。
From the Warring States period through Qin, the sun's precessional displacement amounted to three degrees. In the xinwei year, the seventeenth year of the First Emperor, the winter solstice should fall at twenty-two degrees of Dipper. The Qin calendar's epoch falls on the jisi new moon of the first month, with Establishment of Spring at the first light of dawn; sun, moon, and the five planets all rise at five degrees of Encampment, and the first days of each obscuration cycle align with the four cardinal months. If the new moon hypothetically retreats fifteen days, the intercalary month falls before the first month. If the new moon advances fifteen days, the intercalary month falls after the first month. Thus all twelve solar terms fall within the cycle of expansion and contraction, and the dawn and dusk lodge degrees shift accordingly. Projecting from the twelve solar terms using the Zhuanxu calendar according to the Monthly Ordinances, the result agrees with what Lü Buwei recorded. Yet Ying Ziyan and others hold that the Monthly Ordinances' dawn-and-dusk lodge distances should fall at mid-term qi, making the rain-prayer ceremony too late and contradicting Master Zuo's text; Du Yu also rejects the Monthly Ordinances on the basis of Spring and Autumn. All of these views are wrong. The Liang Datong calendar places the winter solstice at the start of Ox Leader in early Xia times, treating the Bright Hall and Monthly Ordinances as Xia-era records; projecting by mid-term qi does not agree—only by taking the interval between mid-terms as the standard does it come close. They fail to see that placing the reckoning at the start of the solar term naturally brings agreement. From early Qin to the present, another thousand years have passed, and the lodges at the start of solar terms now all fall at mid-term qi. Chunfeng therefore argues, "At mid-spring's mid-term qi today, the sun is at Encampment, and the stars culminating at dusk and dawn differ not at all from the Monthly Ordinances." Examining the Qin calendar, at Establishment of Spring the sun stands at five degrees of Encampment. The Linde calendar has the sun reach Encampment only on Awakening of Insects; its dusk-and-dawn culminating lodges differ by twelve Establishments, yet its authors think there is no error—this is absurd.
57
古曆，冬至昏明中星去日九十二度，春分、秋分百度，夏至百一十八度，率一氣差三度，九日差一刻。
The ancient calendar places stars culminating at dusk and dawn ninety-two degrees from the sun at winter solstice, one hundred degrees at the spring and autumn equinoxes, and one hundred eighteen degrees at summer solstice—on average three degrees per qi, or one quarter-day every nine days.
58
秦曆十二次，立春在營室五度，於太初星距危十六度少也。 昏，畢八度中，月令參中，謂肩股也。 晨，心八度中，月令尾中，於太初星距尾也。 仲春昏，東井十四度中，月令弧中，弧星入東井十八度。 晨，南斗二度中，月令建星中，於太初星距西建也。 甄耀度及魯曆，南方有狼、弧，無東井、鬼，北方有建星，無南斗，井、斗度長，弧、建度短，故以正昏明云。
In the Qin calendar's twelve stations, Establishment of Spring falls at five degrees of Encampment—in the Taichu reckoning the star's distance from Rooftop was a little less than sixteen degrees. At dusk Net stands at eight degrees; the Monthly Ordinances' "Shen at culmination" refers to its shoulder and thigh. At dawn Heart stands at eight degrees; the Monthly Ordinances' "Tail at culmination" refers, in the Taichu reckoning, to the star's distance from Tail. At mid-spring dusk Eastern Well stands at fourteen degrees; the Monthly Ordinances' "Bow at culmination" means the Bow star enters Eastern Well at eighteen degrees. At dawn Southern Dipper stands at two degrees; the Monthly Ordinances' "Establishment at culmination" refers, in the Taichu reckoning, to the star's distance from western Establishment. The Zhenyao degrees and the Lu calendar place Wolf and Bow in the south rather than Eastern Well and Ghost, and Establishment in the north rather than Southern Dipper; Well and Dipper have long degrees while Bow and Establishment have short ones—hence they speak of correcting dusk and dawn reckoning.
59
古曆星度及漢落下閎等所測，其星距遠近不同，然二十八之宿體不異。 古以牽牛上星為距，太初改用中星，入古曆牽牛太半度，於氣法當三十二分日之二十一。 故洪範傳冬至日在牽牛一度，減太初星距二十一分，直南斗二十六度十九分也。 顓頊曆立春起營室五度，冬至在牽牛一度少。 洪範傳冬至所起無餘分，故立春在營室四度太。 祖沖之自營室五度，以太初星距命之，因云秦曆冬至，日在牽牛六度。 虞𠠎等襲沖之之誤，為之說云：「夏時冬至，日在斗末，以歲差考之，牽牛六度乃顓頊之代。 漢時雖覺其差，頓移五度，故冬至還在牛初。 」按洪範古今星距，僅差四分之三，皆起牽牛一度。 𠠎等所說，亦非是。 魯宣公十五年，丁卯歲，顓頊曆第十三蔀首與麟德曆俱以丁巳平旦立春。 至始皇三十三年丁亥，凡三百八十歲，得顓頊曆壬申蔀首。 是歲秦曆以壬申寅初立春，而開元曆與麟德曆俱以庚午平旦，差二日，日當在南斗二十二度。 古曆後天二日，又增二度。 然則秦曆冬至，定在牛前二度。 氣後天二日，日不及天二度，微而難覺，故呂氏循用之。
The star degrees of the ancient calendar and those measured by Luoxia Hong and others of the Han differ in the near and far distances of their reference stars, yet the bodies of the twenty-eight lodges remain the same. Antiquity used Ox Leader's upper star as the reference point; the Taichu calendar switched to the median star, entering the ancient reckoning at one and a half degrees of Ox Leader—in qi computation this equals twenty-one thirty-seconds of a day. The Hongfan commentary therefore places the winter solstice at one degree of Ox Leader; subtracting twenty-one parts from the Taichu star distance, it aligns directly with twenty-six degrees and nineteen parts of Southern Dipper. The Zhuanxu calendar begins Establishment of Spring at five degrees of Encampment, with the winter solstice at a little less than one degree of Ox Leader. The Hongfan commentary's winter solstice starting point has no fractional remainder; Establishment of Spring therefore falls at a little more than four degrees of Encampment. Zu Chongzhi, starting from five degrees of Encampment and naming it by the Taichu star distance, therefore says that in the Qin calendar the winter solstice sun stands at six degrees of Ox Leader. Yu Xi and others followed Chongzhi's error, arguing: "In Xia times the winter solstice sun stood at the Dipper's end; corrected for precession, six degrees of Ox Leader belongs to the Zhuanxu era." In Han times, though they noticed the discrepancy, they abruptly shifted five degrees, so the winter solstice still fell at the start of the Ox. Examining the Hongfan's ancient and modern star distances, they differ by only three-quarters of a part; both start from one degree of Ox Leader. What Yu Xi and others say is also incorrect. In the fifteenth year of Duke Xuan of Lu, the dingmao year, the thirteenth obscuration head of the Zhuanxu calendar and the Linde calendar both place Establishment of Spring at dingsi at level dawn. By the thirty-third year of the First Emperor, dinghai—a span of 380 years—one reaches the renshen obscuration head of the Zhuanxu calendar. That year the Qin calendar places Establishment of Spring at renshen at the start of yin, while the Kaiyuan and Linde calendars both use gengwu at level dawn—two days apart; the sun should stand at twenty-two degrees of Southern Dipper. The ancient calendar lags heaven by two days and adds two degrees. The Qin calendar's winter solstice, then, is fixed at two degrees before the Ox. The qi lags heaven by two days and the sun falls short of heaven by two degrees—subtle and hard to notice—so Lü's Annals continued to use it.
60
及漢興，張蒼等亦以為顓頊曆比五家疎闊中最近密。 今考月蝕衝，則開元冬至，上及牛初正差一次。 淳風以為古術疎舛，雖弦望、昏明，差天十五度而猶不知。 又引呂氏春秋，黃帝以仲春乙卯日在奎，始奏十二鍾，命之曰咸池。 至今三千餘年，而春分亦在奎，反謂秦曆與今不異。 按不韋所記，以其月令孟春在奎，謂黃帝之時亦在奎，猶淳風曆冬至斗十三度，因謂黃帝時亦在建星耳。 經籍所載，合於歲差者，淳風皆不取，而專取於呂氏春秋。 若謂十二紀可以為正，則立春在營室五度，固當不易，安得頓移，使當啟蟄之節？ 此又其所不思也。
When Han rose, Zhang Cang and others also held that among the five schools' crude methods, the Zhuanxu calendar was the nearest and most precise. Examined now by lunar eclipse opposition, the Kaiyuan winter solstice, projected backward, reaches the start of the Ox—exactly one station off. Chunfeng holds that ancient methods are crude and erroneous—even for quarter moons, full and new moons, and dusk and dawn they could be fifteen degrees off heaven without realizing it. He also cites Lü's Spring and Autumn Annals: the Yellow Emperor, on the yimao day of mid-spring with the sun in Straddler, first performed the twelve bells and named them Xianchi. More than 3,000 years have passed, yet the spring equinox is also in Straddler; he instead claims the Qin calendar does not differ from the present. Examining what Lü Buwei recorded: because his Monthly Ordinances places first spring in Straddler, he claims the Yellow Emperor's era was also in Straddler—just as Chunfeng's calendar places the winter solstice at thirteen degrees of Dipper and therefore claims the Yellow Emperor's era was also at Establishment. What the classics record that agrees with precession, Chunfeng rejects entirely, relying exclusively on Lü's Spring and Autumn Annals. If one claims the twelve chronicles can serve as the standard, then Establishment of Spring at five degrees of Encampment should be unchanging—how can it abruptly shift to fall on Awakening of Insects? This too is what he fails to consider.
61
漢四百二十六年，日却差五度。 景帝中元三年甲午歲冬至，應在斗二十一度。
Over the 426 years of the Han dynasty, the sun's precessional displacement amounted to five degrees. In the jiawu year, the third year of Emperor Jing's Zhongyuan reign, the winter solstice should fall at twenty-one degrees of Dipper.
62
太初元年，三統曆及周曆皆以十一月夜半合朔冬至，日月俱起牽牛一度。 古曆與近代密率相較，二百年氣差一日，三百年朔差一日。 推而上之，久益先天； 引而下之，久益後天。 僖公五年，周曆正月辛亥朔，餘四分之一，南至。 以歲差推之，日在牽牛初。 至宣公十一年癸亥，周曆與麟德曆俱以庚戌日中冬至，而月朔尚先麟德曆十五辰。 至昭公二十年己卯，周曆以正月己丑朔日中南至，麟德曆以己丑平旦冬至。 哀公十一年丁巳，周曆入己酉蔀首，麟德曆以戊申禺中冬至。 惠王四十三年己丑，周曆入丁卯蔀首，麟德曆以乙丑日昳冬至。 呂后八年辛酉，周曆入乙酉蔀首，麟德曆以壬午黃昏冬至； 其十二月甲申，人定合朔。 太初元年，周曆以甲子夜半合朔冬至，麟德曆以辛酉禺中冬至，十二月癸亥晡時合朔。 氣差三十二辰，朔差四辰。 此疎密之大較也。
In Taichu 1, the Triple Concordance and Zhou calendars both place the eleventh-month midnight new moon and winter solstice together, with sun and moon both rising at one degree of Ox Leader. Compared with recent precise rates, the ancient calendar drifts one day in qi over two hundred years and one day in new moons over three hundred years. Projected backward, over time it increasingly runs ahead of heaven; projected forward, over time it increasingly lags behind heaven. In Duke Xi's fifth year, the Zhou calendar's first-month xinhai new moon, with a remainder of one-quarter, marks the winter solstice. Calculated with precession, the sun stood at the start of Ox Leader. By Duke Xuan's eleventh year, guihai, the Zhou and Linde calendars both place the winter solstice at gengxu midday, yet the monthly new moon still precedes the Linde calendar by fifteen chen. By Duke Zhao's twentieth year, jimao, the Zhou calendar places the winter solstice at midday on the jichou new moon of the first month, while the Linde calendar places it at level dawn on jichou. In Duke Ai's eleventh year, dingsi, the Zhou calendar enters the jiyou obscuration head, while the Linde calendar places the winter solstice at wushen mid-morning. In King Hui's forty-third year, jichou, the Zhou calendar enters the dingmao obscuration head, while the Linde calendar places the winter solstice at yichou mid-afternoon. In Empress Lü's eighth year, xinyou, the Zhou calendar enters the yiyou obscuration head, while the Linde calendar places the winter solstice at renwu dusk; on the jiashen day of the twelfth month, the new moon falls at human settlement. In Taichu 1, the Zhou calendar places the midnight jiazi new moon and winter solstice together, while the Linde calendar places the winter solstice at xinyou mid-morning and the twelfth-month new moon at guihai late afternoon. The qi differ by thirty-two chen and the new moons by four chen. This is the broad comparison of crude versus precise reckoning.
63
僖公五年，周曆、漢曆、唐曆皆以辛亥南至。 後五百五十餘歲，至太初元年，周曆、漢曆皆得甲子夜半冬至，唐曆皆以辛酉，則漢曆後天三日矣。 祖沖之、張冑玄促上章歲至太初元年，沖之以癸亥雞鳴冬至，而冑玄以癸亥日出。 欲令合於甲子，而適與魯曆相會。 自此推僖公五年，魯曆以庚戌冬至，而二家皆以甲寅。 且僖公登觀臺以望而書雲物，出於表晷天驗，非時史億度。 乖丘明正時之意，以就劉歆之失。 今考麟德元年甲子，唐曆皆以甲子冬至，而周曆、漢曆皆以庚午。 然則自太初下至麟德差四日，自太初上及僖公差三日，不足疑也。
In Duke Xi's fifth year, the Zhou, Han, and Tang calendars all place the winter solstice on xinhai. More than 550 years later, by Taichu 1, the Zhou and Han calendars both place the winter solstice at midnight on jiazi, while the Tang calendar uses xinyou—the Han calendar thus lags heaven by three days. Zu Chongzhi and Zhang Zhouxuan shortened the superior cycle year to reach Taichu 1; Chongzhi places the winter solstice at guihai cockcrow, while Zhouxuan places it at guihai sunrise. They wished to make it agree with jiazi and thereby coincide with the Lu calendar. Projecting back from this to Duke Xi's fifth year, the Lu calendar places the winter solstice on gengxu, while both schools use jiayin. Moreover, Duke Xi ascended the observation tower to observe and record cloud signs—this came from gnomon and sundial verification by heaven, not the calendar officer's guesswork. This departs from Qiu Ming's intent to correct the seasons, accommodating Liu Xin's error. Examining Linde 1, jiazi: the Tang calendar places the winter solstice on jiazi, while the Zhou and Han calendars both use gengwu. From Taichu down to Linde the difference is four days; from Taichu back to Duke Xi it is three days—not enough to raise doubt.
64
以歲差考太初元年辛酉冬至加時，日在斗二十三度。 漢曆，氣後天三日，而日先天三度，所差尚少。 故落下閎等雖候昏明中星，步日所在，猶未覺其差。 然洪範、太初所揆，冬至昏奎八度中，夏至昏氐十三度中，依漢曆，冬至，日在牽牛初太半度，以昏距中命之，奎十一度中； 夏至，房一度中。 此皆閎等所測，自差三度，則劉向等殆已知太初冬至不及天三度矣。
Examined with precession, at the added hour of the xinyou winter solstice in Taichu 1 the sun stood at twenty-three degrees of Dipper. In the Han calendar, qi lags heaven by three days while the sun leads heaven by three degrees—the discrepancy is still small. Luoxia Hong and others, though they observed stars culminating at dusk and dawn and calculated the sun's position, still did not notice the discrepancy. Yet what the Hongfan and Taichu measured places Straddler at eight degrees at winter-solstice dusk and Root at thirteen degrees at summer-solstice dusk. By the Han calendar, at winter solstice the sun stands at a little more than the start of Ox Leader; named by dusk distance to culmination, Straddler stands at eleven degrees; at summer solstice Room stands at one degree. These were all measured by Luoxia Hong and his colleagues; differing by three degrees on their own—Liu Xiang and others probably already knew that the Taichu winter solstice fell short of heaven by three degrees.
65
及永平中，治曆者考行事，史官注日，常不及太初曆五度。 然諸儒守讖緯，以為當在牛初，故賈逵等議：「石氏星距，黃道規牽牛初直斗二十度，於赤道二十一度也。 尚書考靈耀斗二十二度，無餘分。 冬至，日在牽牛初，無牽牛所起文。 編訢等據今日所去牽牛中星五度，於斗二十一度四分一，與考靈耀相近。 」遂更曆從斗二十一度起。 然古曆以斗魁首為距，至牽牛為二十二度，未聞移牽牛六度以就太初星距也。 逵等以末學僻於所傳，而昧天象，故以權誣之，而後聽從他術，以為日在牛初者，由此遂黜。
By the Yongping era, calendar makers examining actual events found the historiographers' recorded days regularly fell five degrees short of the Taichu calendar. Yet the scholars clung to apocryphal texts and prognostications, believing the winter solstice should fall at the start of the Ox; Jia Kui and others therefore argued, "Master Shi's star distance: from the start of Ox Leader on the ecliptic circle the alignment runs directly to twenty degrees of Dipper—twenty-one degrees on the equator." The Investiture of the Documents' Examination of Spiritual Radiance gives twenty-two degrees of Dipper, with no fractional remainder. At winter solstice the sun stands at the start of Ox Leader—though there is no text specifying where Ox Leader begins. Bian Xin and others, based on today's five-degree distance from Ox Leader's median star, place it at twenty-one and a quarter degrees of Dipper—close to the Examination of Spiritual Radiance. They therefore revised the calendar to start from twenty-one degrees of Dipper. Yet the ancient calendar used the Dipper's ladle head as reference; to Ox Leader is twenty-two degrees—never has one heard of shifting Ox Leader six degrees to match the Taichu star distance. Kui and others, late learners narrow in what was transmitted and ignorant of celestial signs, therefore used expedient falsehood; afterward, accepting other methods that placed the sun at the start of the Ox, this view was dismissed.
66
今歲差，引而退之，則辛酉冬至，日在斗二十度，合於密率，而有驗於今。 推而進之，則甲子冬至，日在斗二十四度，昏奎八度中，而有證於古。 其虛退之度，又適及牽牛之初。 而沖之雖促減氣分，冀符漢曆，猶差六度，未及於天。 而麟德曆冬至不移，則昏中向差半次。 淳風以為太初元年得本星度，日月合璧，俱起建星。 賈逵考曆，亦云古曆冬至皆起建星。 兩漢冬至，日皆後天，故其宿度多在斗末。 今以儀測，建星在斗十三四度間，自古冬至無差，審矣。
With precession now, drawing back and retreating, the xinyou winter solstice places the sun at twenty degrees of Dipper—agreeing with the precise rate and verified in the present. Projecting forward, the jiazi winter solstice places the sun at twenty-four degrees of Dipper, with Straddler at eight degrees at dusk culmination—confirmed by antiquity. The degrees of void retreat also just reach the start of Ox Leader. Yet though Chongzhi shortened and reduced the qi fraction, hoping to match the Han calendar, it still differed by six degrees—falling short of heaven. Yet the Linde calendar's winter solstice does not shift; dusk culmination then differs by half a station. Chunfeng believes Taichu 1 recovered the original star degrees, with sun and moon conjoined and both rising at Establishment. Jia Kui, examining calendars, also says ancient calendars all place the winter solstice at Establishment. In both Han dynasties the winter solstice sun lagged heaven; therefore its lodge degrees mostly fell at the Dipper's end. Measured now with instruments, Establishment lies between thirteen and fourteen degrees of Dipper; from antiquity the winter solstice has not shifted—this is confirmed.
67
按古之六術，並同四分。 四分之法，久則後天。 推古曆之作，皆在漢初，却較春秋，朔並先天，則非三代之前明矣。
Examining the ancient six methods, all agree with the Quarter Remainder system. The Quarter Remainder method, given enough time, lags behind heaven. Projecting the composition of ancient calendars, all date to early Han; compared back to Spring and Autumn, their new moons all run ahead of heaven—clearly not from before the Three Dynasties.
68
古曆，南斗至牽牛上星二十一度，入太初星距四度，上直西建之初。 故六家或以南斗命度，或以建星命度。 方周、漢之交，日已潛退，其襲春秋舊曆者，則以為在牽牛之首； 其考當時之驗者，則以為入建星度中。 然氣朔前後不逾一日，故漢曆冬至，當在斗末。 以為建星上得太初本星度，此其明據也。 四分法雖疎，而先賢謹於天事，其遷革之意，俱有効於當時，故太史公等觀二十八宿疎密，立晷儀，下漏刻，以稽晦朔、分至、躔離、弦望，其赤道遺法，後世無以非之。 故雜候清臺，太初最密。 若當時日在建星，已直斗十三度，則壽王調曆宜允得其中，豈容頓差一氣而未知其謬，不能觀乎時變，而欲厚誣古人也。
The ancient calendar: from Southern Dipper to Ox Leader's upper star is twenty-one degrees; entering the Taichu star distance four degrees, it aligns directly with the start of western Establishment. Therefore the six schools either name degrees from Southern Dipper or from Establishment. At the junction of Zhou and Han the sun had silently retreated; those inheriting the Spring and Autumn old calendar placed it at the head of Ox Leader; those examining contemporary verification placed it within the degrees of Establishment. Yet qi and new moons differ by no more than a day either way; the Han calendar's winter solstice should therefore fall at the Dipper's end. That Establishment obtains the Taichu original star degrees is the clear evidence. Though the Quarter Remainder method is crude, the ancients were careful in celestial affairs, and their revisions were effective for their time. Grand Historian Sima Qian and others observed the density and sparsity of the twenty-eight lodges, set up gnomon instruments, and installed clepsydra marks to verify new and full moons, equinoxes and solstices, planetary progressions, and quarter moons—their equatorial legacy, which later ages have no grounds to reject. Among mixed observations at the Clear Terrace, Taichu was the most precise. If at that time the sun at Establishment already aligned directly with thirteen degrees of Dipper, then Shou Wang's calendar adjustment should have hit the mark—how could it abruptly differ by one qi without recognizing the error, fail to observe temporal change, and yet seek to slander the ancients?
69
後百餘歲，至永平十一年，以麟德曆較之，氣當後天二日半，朔當後天半日。 是歲四分曆得辛酉蔀首，已減太初曆四分日之三，定後天二日太半。 開元曆以戊午禺中冬至，日在斗十八度半弱，潛退至牛前八度。 進至辛酉夜半，日在斗二十一度半弱。 續漢志云：「元和二年冬至，日在斗二十一度四分之一。 」是也。
More than a hundred years later, by Yongping 11, compared with the Linde calendar, qi should lag heaven by two and a half days and new moons by half a day. That year the Quarter Remainder calendar reaches the xinyou obscuration head, having already reduced the Taichu calendar by three-quarters of a day and fixed the lag behind heaven at two and a half days. The Kaiyuan calendar places the winter solstice at wuwu mid-morning, with the sun at eighteen and a half degrees weak of Dipper, silently retreated to eight degrees before the Ox. Advancing to xinyou midnight, the sun stands at twenty-one and a half degrees weak of Dipper. The Continued Han Treatise says, "In Yuanhe 2 the winter solstice sun stood at twenty-one and a quarter degrees of Dipper." That is correct.
70
祖沖之曰：「四分曆立冬景長一丈，立春九尺六寸，冬至南極日晷最長。 二氣去至日數既同，則中景應等。 而相差四寸，此冬至後天之驗也。 二氣中景，日差九分半弱，進退調均，略無盈縮。 各退二日十二刻，則景皆九尺八寸。 以此推冬至後天亦二日十二刻矣。 」東漢晷漏定於永元十四年，則四分法施行後十五歲也。
Zu Chongzhi says, "The Quarter Remainder calendar gives a shadow length of one zhang at Establishment of Winter, nine chi six cun at Establishment of Spring, and the longest sundial shadow at the southern extreme on winter solstice." The two qi are equally distant from the solstice days in number; the mid-shadows should therefore be equal. Yet they differ by four cun—this verifies that the winter solstice lags heaven. The two qi's mid-shadows differ daily by nine and a half parts weak; adjusted evenly in advance and retreat, they show roughly no expansion or contraction. Retreat each by two days and twelve marks, and the shadows are all nine chi eight cun. From this one infers that the winter solstice also lags heaven by two days and twelve marks. The Eastern Han gnomon and clepsydra were fixed in Yongyuan 14—fifteen years after the Quarter Remainder method was implemented.
71
二十四氣加時，進退不等，其去午正極遠者四十九刻有餘。 日中之晷，頗有盈縮，故治曆者皆就其中率，以午正言之。 而開元曆所推氣及日度，皆直子半之始。 其未及日中，尚五十刻。 因加二日十二刻，正得二日太半。 與沖之所算及破章二百年間輒差一日之數，皆合。
The added hours of the twenty-four qi advance and retreat unequally; the farthest from noon proper exceeds forty-nine marks. The midday gnomon shadow varies considerably; calendar makers therefore all take the mean rate and speak in terms of noon proper. Yet the Kaiyuan calendar's projected qi and solar degrees all align directly with the start of zi midnight. They have not yet reached midday—still fifty marks short. Adding two days and twelve marks therefore yields exactly two and a half days. This agrees with Chongzhi's calculation and with the rate of one day's difference every two hundred years when breaking the cycle.
72
自漢時辛酉冬至，以後天之數減之，則合於今曆歲差斗十八度。 自今曆戊午冬至，以後天之數加之，則合於賈逵所測斗二十一度。 反復僉同。 而淳風冬至常在斗十三度，豈當時知不及牽牛五度，而不知過建星八度耶？
From the xinyou winter solstice of Han times, subtracting the lag-behind-heaven amount, it agrees with the present calendar's precession at eighteen degrees of Dipper. From the present calendar's wuwu winter solstice, adding the lag-behind-heaven amount, it agrees with Jia Kui's measurement at twenty-one degrees of Dipper. Repeated examination confirms the agreement. Yet Chunfeng's winter solstice constantly falls at thirteen degrees of Dipper—did he know it fell short of Ox Leader by five degrees, yet not know it overshot Establishment by eight degrees?
73
晉武帝太始三年丁亥歲冬至，日當在斗十六度。 晉用魏景初曆，其冬至亦在斗二十一度少。
In the dinghai year, Taishi 3 of Emperor Wu of Jin, the winter solstice sun should stand at sixteen degrees of Dipper. Jin used Wei's Jingchu calendar; its winter solstice also fell at a little less than twenty-one degrees of Dipper.
74
太元九年，姜岌更造三紀術，退在斗十七度。 曰：「古曆斗分彊，故不可施於今； 乾象斗分細，故不可通於古。 景初雖得其中，而日之所在； 乃差四度，合朔虧盈，皆不及其次。 假月在東井一度蝕，以日檢之，乃在參六度。 」岌以月蝕衝知日度，由是躔次遂正，為後代治曆者宗。
In Taiyuan 9 Jiang Ji remade the Three Era method, retreating to seventeen degrees of Dipper. He said, "The ancient calendar's Dipper fraction is too large, so it cannot be applied to the present; the Supernal Icon's Dipper fraction is too fine, so it cannot extend to antiquity. Jingchu though hits the center in one respect, the sun's position differs by four degrees; new moon conjunctions and eclipse phases all miss their proper stations. Suppose the moon eclipses at one degree of Eastern Well; checked against the sun, it is actually at six degrees of Shen. Ji determined solar degrees by lunar eclipse opposition, thereby corrected lodge positions, and became the model for later calendar makers.
75
宋文帝時，何承天上元嘉曆，曰：「四分、景初曆，冬至同在斗二十一度，臣以月蝕檢之，則今應在斗十七度。 又土圭測二至，晷差三日有餘，則天之南至，日在斗十三四度矣。 」事下太史考驗，如承天所上。 以開元曆考元嘉十年冬至，日在斗十四度，與承天所測合。
In Emperor Wen of Song's time, He Chengtian's Yuanjia calendar said, "The Quarter Remainder and Jingchu calendars both place the winter solstice at twenty-one degrees of Dipper; I check by lunar eclipse, and now it should be at seventeen degrees of Dipper." Moreover, measuring the two solstices with the earth gnomon, the shadow lengths differ by more than three days—heaven's south arrival then has the sun at thirteen or fourteen degrees of Dipper. The matter was sent to the Grand Clerk for verification, and the result matched Chengtian's submission. Examined with the Kaiyuan calendar, the Yuanjia 10 winter solstice places the sun at fourteen degrees of Dipper—agreeing with Chengtian's measurement.
76
大明八年，祖沖之上大明曆，冬至在斗十一度，開元曆應在斗十三度。 梁天監八年，沖之子員外散騎侍郎暅之上其家術。 詔太史令將作大匠道秀等較之，上距大明又五十年，日度益差。 其明年，閏月十六日，月蝕，在虛十度，日應在張四度。 承天曆在張六度，沖之曆在張二度。
In Daming 8 Zu Chongzhi submitted the Daming calendar, placing the winter solstice at eleven degrees of Dipper; the Kaiyuan calendar should place it at thirteen degrees of Dipper. In Liang Tianjian 8, Chongzhi's son Xu, Attendant Gentleman of the Exterior and Cavalier Attendant, submitted their family's method. The emperor ordered Grand Clerk and Master of Works Daoxiu and others to compare them; another fifty years above Daming, solar degrees had diverged further. The next year, on the sixteenth day of the intercalary month, a lunar eclipse occurred at ten degrees of Void; the sun should have been at four degrees of Extended Net. The Chengtian calendar places it at six degrees of Extended Net; the Chongzhi calendar at two degrees of Extended Net.
77
大同九年，虞𠠎等議：「姜岌、何承天俱以月蝕衝步日所在。 承天雖移岌三度，然其冬至亦上岌三日。 承天在斗十三四度，而岌在斗十七度。 其實非移。 祖沖之謂為實差，以推今冬至，日在斗九度，用求中星不合。 自岌至今，將二百年，而冬至在斗十二度。 然日之所在難知，驗以中星，則漏刻不定。 漢世課昏明中星，為法已淺。 今候夜半中星，以求日衝，近於得密。 而水有清濁，壺有增減，或積塵所擁，故漏有遲疾。 臣等頻夜候中星，而前後相差或至三度。 大略冬至遠不過斗十四度，近不出十度。 」又以九年三月十五日夜半，月在房四度蝕。 九月十五日夜半，月在昴三度蝕。 以其衝計，冬至皆在斗十二度。 自姜岌、何承天所測，下及大同，日已却差二度。 而淳風以為晉、宋以來三百餘歲，以月蝕衝考之，固在斗十三四度間，非矣。
In Datong 9 Yu Xi and others argued, "Jiang Ji and He Chengtian both calculated the sun's position by lunar eclipse opposition." Chengtian though shifted Ji's reckoning by three degrees, his winter solstice also advances Ji's by three days. Chengtian places it at thirteen or fourteen degrees of Dipper, while Ji at seventeen degrees of Dipper. In fact there was no shift. Zu Chongzhi took it as real divergence; projecting today's winter solstice to nine degrees of Dipper, using this to seek culminating stars, it does not agree. From Ji's time to now, nearly two hundred years, the winter solstice stands at twelve degrees of Dipper. Yet the sun's position is hard to know; verified by culminating stars, the clepsydra marks are uncertain. The Han method of checking dusk-and-dawn culminating stars was already a shallow approach. Observing midnight culminating stars to seek solar opposition comes closer to precision. Yet water varies in clarity, vessels vary in capacity, and dust may accumulate and block them—so the clepsydra runs slow or fast. We repeatedly observed culminating stars at night, yet the difference from one night to the next sometimes reached three degrees. Broadly speaking, the winter solstice at farthest does not exceed fourteen degrees of Dipper; at nearest does not fall below ten degrees. Moreover, at midnight on the fifteenth day of the third month of the ninth year, the moon eclipsed at four degrees of Room. At midnight on the fifteenth day of the ninth month, the moon eclipsed at three degrees of Hairy Head. Calculated by their opposition, the winter solstice falls at twelve degrees of Dipper in both cases. From what Jiang Ji and He Chengtian measured down to Datong, the sun has precessionally shifted two degrees. Yet Chunfeng holds that from Jin and Song across more than three hundred years, examined by lunar eclipse opposition, it firmly lies between thirteen and fourteen degrees of Dipper—that is wrong.
78
劉孝孫甲子元曆，推太初冬至在牽牛初，下及晉太元、宋元嘉皆在斗十七度。 開皇十四年，在斗十三度。 而劉焯曆仁壽四年冬至，日在黃道斗十度，於赤道斗十一度也。 其後孝孫改從焯法，而仁壽四年冬至，日亦在斗十度。 焯卒後，冑玄以其前曆上元起虛五度，推漢太初，猶不及牽牛，乃更起虛七度，故太初在斗二十三度，永平在斗二十一度，並與今曆合。 而仁壽四年，冬至在斗十三度，以驗近事，又不逮其前曆矣。 戊寅曆，太初元年辛酉冬至，進及甲子，日在牽牛三度。 永平十一年，得戊午冬至，進及辛酉，在斗二十六度。 至元嘉，中氣上景初三日，而冬至猶在斗十七度。 欲以求合，反更失之。 又曲循孝孫之論，而不知孝孫已變從皇極，故為淳風等所駁。 歲差之術，由此不行。
Liu Xiaosun's Jiazi Origin calendar projects the Taichu winter solstice at the start of Ox Leader; down through Jin Taiyuan and Song Yuanjia all at seventeen degrees of Dipper. In Kaihuang 14 it stood at thirteen degrees of Dipper. Yet Liu Chuo's calendar for the Renshou 4 winter solstice places the sun at ten degrees of ecliptic Dipper—eleven degrees of equatorial Dipper. Afterward Xiaosun changed to follow Chuo's method; the Renshou 4 winter solstice also places the sun at ten degrees of Dipper. After Chuo died, Zhouxuan's earlier calendar started its epoch at five degrees of Void; projecting back to Han Taichu it still did not reach Ox Leader, so he restarted at seven degrees of Void—thus Taichu at twenty-three degrees of Dipper and Yongping at twenty-one degrees, both agreeing with the present calendar. Yet the Renshou 4 winter solstice at thirteen degrees of Dipper—verified against recent events—again falls short of his earlier calendar. The Wuyin calendar places Taichu 1 xinyou winter solstice, advancing to jiazi, with the sun at three degrees of Ox Leader. Yongping 11 yields wuwu winter solstice, advancing to xinyou, at twenty-six degrees of Dipper. By Yuanjia the mid-term qi's upper shadow length differed by three days, yet the winter solstice still stood at seventeen degrees of Dipper. Seeking agreement, one instead loses further ground. Moreover, bending to follow Xiaosun's doctrine without knowing Xiaosun had already changed to follow the Huangji calendar—therefore refuted by Chunfeng and others. The method of precession thereby failed to prevail.
79
以太史注記月蝕衝考日度，麟德元年九月庚申，月蝕在婁十度。 至開元四年六月庚申，月蝕在牛六度。 較麟德曆率差三度，則今冬至定在赤道斗十度。
Examining solar degrees by the Grand Clerk's recorded lunar eclipse oppositions: in Linde 1, on gengshen of the ninth month, a lunar eclipse occurred at ten degrees of Encampment. By Kaiyuan 4, on gengshen of the sixth month, a lunar eclipse occurred at six degrees of Ox. Compared with the Linde calendar's rate, a difference of three degrees fixes today's winter solstice at ten degrees of equatorial Dipper.
80
又皇極曆歲差皆自黃道命之，其每歲周分，常當南至之軌，與赤道相較，所減尤多。 計黃道差三十六度，赤道差四十餘度，雖每歲遯之，不足為過。 然立法之體，宜盡其原，是以開元曆皆自赤道推之，乃以今有術從變黃道。
Moreover, the Huangji calendar names precession entirely from the ecliptic; its yearly circuit fraction, corresponding to the south-arrival track, subtracts especially much when compared with the equator. Calculated, the ecliptic difference is thirty-six degrees and the equatorial difference more than forty degrees—though retreated each year, this is not excessive. Yet the substance of establishing law should exhaust its origin; the Kaiyuan calendar therefore projects entirely from the equator, then uses present methods to transform to the ecliptic.
81
校勘記0.85em|columns=2
Collation note (editorial markup: 0.85em|columns=2).
82
其八日躔盈縮略例曰：
The eighth section, Summary Principles of Lodge Motion and Expansion-Contraction, says:
83
北齊張子信積候合蝕加時，覺日行有入氣差，然損益未得其正。 至劉焯，立盈縮躔衰術，與四象升降。 麟德曆因之，更名躔差。 凡陰陽往來，皆馴積而變。 日南至，其行最急，急而漸損，至春分及中而後遲。 迨日北至，其行最舒，而漸益之，以至秋分又及中而後益急。 急極而寒若，舒極而燠若，及中而雨暘之氣交，自然之數也。 焯術於春分前一日最急，後一日最舒； 秋分前一日最舒，後一日最急。 舒急同于二至，而中間一日平行。 其說非是。 當以二十四氣晷景，考日躔盈縮而密於加時。
Northern Qi's Zhang Zixin, accumulating observations and combining eclipse added hours, perceived that the sun's motion had qi-entry discrepancy, yet the increase and decrease did not obtain the correct value. Liu Chuo established expansion-contraction lodge-decline methods, paired with the four images' ascent and descent. The Linde calendar followed this, renaming it lodge difference. All yin and yang coming and going change through gradual accumulation. At the winter solstice its motion is swiftest; swift then gradually diminishing, until the spring equinox reaches the center and afterward slows. By the summer solstice its motion is most relaxed; gradually increasing until the autumn equinox again reaches the center and afterward grows swifter. Swift to the extreme and cold sets in; relaxed to the extreme and warmth sets in; at the center rain and clear weather exchange—this is nature's rhythm. Chuo's method makes the day before the spring equinox the swiftest and the day after the most relaxed; the day before the autumn equinox the most relaxed and the day after the swiftest. Relaxed and swift match the two solstices, while the middle day moves uniformly. This doctrine is incorrect. One should examine the sun's expansion and contraction by the gnomon shadows of the twenty-four qi, making added hours more precise.
84
其九九道議曰：
Its Nine Paths discourse says:
85
洪範傳云：「日有中道，月有九行。 」中道，謂黃道也。 九行者，青道二，出黃道東； 朱道二，出黃道南； 白道二，出黃道西； 黑道二，出黃道北。 立春、春分，月東從青道； 立夏、夏至，月南從朱道； 立秋、秋分，月西從白道； 立冬、冬至，月北從黑道。 漢史官舊事，九道術廢久，劉洪頗採以著遲疾陰陽曆，然本以消息為奇，而術不傳。
The Hongfan commentary says, "The sun has a central path; the moon has nine courses." The central path means the ecliptic. The nine courses are: two green courses, emerging east of the ecliptic; two vermilion courses, emerging south of the ecliptic; two white courses, emerging west of the ecliptic; two black courses, emerging north of the ecliptic. At Establishment of Spring and the spring equinox, the moon follows the green course eastward; At Establishment of Summer and the summer solstice, the moon follows the vermilion course southward; At Establishment of Autumn and the autumn equinox, the moon follows the white course westward; At Establishment of Winter and the winter solstice, the moon follows the black course northward. Han historiographers' old records show the Nine Paths method long abandoned; Liu Hong considerably adopted it to compose the Slow-Fast Yin-Yang calendar, yet it originally took waxing-waning as its marvel, and the method was not transmitted.
86
推陰陽曆交在冬至、夏至，則月行青道、白道，所交則同，而出入之行異。 故青道至春分之宿，及其所衝，皆在黃道正東； 白道至秋分之宿，及其所衝，皆在黃道正西。 若陰陽曆交在立春、立秋，則月循朱道、黑道，所交則同，而出入之行異。 故朱道至立夏之宿，及其所衝，皆在黃道西南； 黑道至立冬之宿，及其所衝，皆在黃道東北。 若陰陽曆交在春分、秋分之宿，則月行朱道、黑道，所交則同，而出入之行異。 故朱道至夏至之宿，及其所衝，皆在黃道正南； 黑道至冬至之宿，及其所衝，皆在黃道正北。 若陰陽曆交在立夏、立冬，則月循青道、白道，所交則同，而出入之行異。 故青道至立春之宿，及其所衝，皆在黃道東南； 白道至立秋之宿，及其所衝，皆在黃道西北。 其大紀皆兼二道，而實分主八節，合于四正四維。
In the Yin-Yang calendar, when conjunction falls at the winter and summer solstices, the moon travels the green and white courses—the conjunctions are the same, yet the entering and exiting courses differ. Therefore the green course reaches the spring equinox lodge and its opposition—all lie directly east of the ecliptic; the white course reaches the autumn equinox lodge and its opposition—all lie directly west of the ecliptic. If the Yin-Yang calendar's conjunction falls at Establishment of Spring and Establishment of Autumn, the moon follows the vermilion and black courses—the conjunctions are the same, yet the entering and exiting courses differ. Therefore the vermilion course reaches the Establishment of Summer lodge and its opposition—all lie southwest of the ecliptic; the black course reaches the Establishment of Winter lodge and its opposition—all lie northeast of the ecliptic. If the Yin-Yang calendar's conjunction falls at the spring and autumn equinox lodges, the moon travels the vermilion and black courses—the conjunctions are the same, yet the entering and exiting courses differ. Therefore the vermilion course reaches the summer solstice lodge and its opposition—all lie directly south of the ecliptic; the black course reaches the winter solstice lodge and its opposition—all lie directly north of the ecliptic. If the Yin-Yang calendar's conjunction falls at Establishment of Summer and Establishment of Winter, the moon follows the green and white courses—the conjunctions are the same, yet the entering and exiting courses differ. Therefore the green course reaches the Establishment of Spring lodge and its opposition—all lie southeast of the ecliptic; the white course reaches the Establishment of Autumn lodge and its opposition—all lie northwest of the ecliptic. Their great cycles all combine two courses, yet in fact each governs eight nodes, matching the four cardinals and four intercardinals.
87
按陰陽曆中終之所交，則月行正當黃道，去交七日，其行九十一度，齊於一象之率，而得八行之中。 八行與中道而九，是謂九道。 凡八行正於春秋，其去黃道六度，則交在冬夏； 正於冬夏，其去黃道六度，則交在春秋。 易九六、七八，迭為終始之象也。 乾坤定位，則八行各當其正。 及其寒暑相推，晦朔相易，則在南者變而居北，在東者徙而為西，屈伸、消息之象也。
At the Yin-Yang calendar's midpoint conjunction, the moon travels directly along the ecliptic; seven days from conjunction it covers ninety-one degrees, matching one quadrant's rate and reaching the center of the eight courses. The eight courses plus the central course make nine—this is what is called the nine courses. When the eight courses align with spring and autumn, six degrees from the ecliptic, conjunction falls in winter and summer; When they align with winter and summer, six degrees from the ecliptic, conjunction falls in spring and autumn. In the Changes, nine and six, seven and eight alternately embody the images of ending and beginning. With qian and kun fixed in position, each of the eight courses holds its proper place. As cold and heat succeed each other and dark and new moon alternate, what was south turns north, what was east shifts west—the images of bending and extending, waxing and waning.
88
黃道之差，始自春分、秋分，赤道所交前後各五度為限。 初，黃道增多赤道二十四分之十二，每限損一，極九限，數終于四，率赤道四十五度而黃道四十八度，至四立之際，一度少強，依平。 復從四起，初限五度，赤道增多黃道二十四分之四，每限益一，極九限而止，終于十二，率赤道四十五度而黃道四十二度，復得冬、夏至之中矣。
The ecliptic's deviation begins at the spring and autumn equinoxes, with five degrees before and after the equatorial junction as the limit. At first the ecliptic exceeds the equator by twelve parts in twenty-four; each limit decreases by one, up to nine limits; the count ends at four—per forty-five equatorial degrees the ecliptic is forty-eight degrees; at the four Establishments it is a degree and a fraction less, then evens out. Starting again from four, the initial limit is five degrees; the equator exceeds the ecliptic by four parts in twenty-four; each limit increases by one, up to nine limits; ending at twelve—per forty-five equatorial degrees the ecliptic is forty-two degrees, restoring the midpoint of the winter and summer solstices.
89
月道之差，始自交初、交中，黃道所交亦距交前後五度為限。 初限，月道增多黃道四十八分之十二，每限損一，極九限而止，數終于四，率黃道四十五度而月道四十六度半，乃一度強，依平。 復從四起，初限五度，月道差少黃道四十八分之四，每限益一，極九限而止，終于十二，率黃道四十五度而月道四十三度半，至陰陽曆二交之半矣。 凡近交初限增十二分者，至半交末限減十二分，去交四十六度得損益之平率。
The lunar path's deviation begins at initial and middle conjunction; the ecliptic junction likewise takes five degrees before and after conjunction as the limit. At the initial limit, the lunar path exceeds the ecliptic by twelve parts in forty-eight; each limit decreases by one, up to nine limits; the count ends at four—per forty-five ecliptic degrees the lunar path is forty-six and a half degrees, a full degree more, then evens out. Starting again from four, the initial limit is five degrees; the lunar path falls short of the ecliptic by four parts in forty-eight; each limit increases by one, up to nine limits; ending at twelve—per forty-five ecliptic degrees the lunar path is forty-three and a half degrees, reaching the midpoint of the Yin-Yang calendar's two conjunctions. Wherever twelve parts in forty-eight are added at the near initial limit, twelve parts in forty-eight are subtracted at the half-conjunction final limit; at forty-six degrees from conjunction one obtains the balanced rate of increase and decrease.
90
夫日行與歲差偕遷，月行隨交限而變，遯伏相消，朓朒相補，則九道之數可知矣。 其月道所交與二分同度，則赤道、黑道近交初限，黃道增二十四分之十二，月道增四十八分之十二。 至半交之末，其減亦如之。 故於九限之際，黃道差三度，月道差一度半，蓋損益之數齊也。 若所交與四立同度，則黃道在損益之中，月道差四十八分之十二。 月道至損益之中，黃道差二十四分之十二。 於九限之際，黃道差三度，月道差四分度之三，皆朓朒相補也。 若所交與二至同度，則青道、白道近交初限，黃道減二十四分之十二，月道增四十八分之十二。 至半交之末，黃道增二十四分之十二，月道減四十八分之十二。 於九限之際，黃道與月道差同，蓋遯伏相消也。
The sun's daily path shifts with the annual difference; the moon's path changes with the conjunction limits; retreat and hiding cancel out, waxing and waning compensate—then the numbers of the nine courses can be known. When the lunar path's conjunction coincides with the two equinoxes, at the near initial limit of the equator and black course the ecliptic increases by twelve parts in twenty-four and the lunar path by twelve parts in forty-eight. At the end of the half conjunction, the decrease is the same. Thus at the nine limits the ecliptic differs by three degrees and the lunar path by one and a half degrees—for the numbers of increase and decrease are equal. If the conjunction coincides with the four Establishments, the ecliptic is at the midpoint of increase and decrease, and the lunar path differs by twelve parts in forty-eight. When the lunar path reaches the midpoint of increase and decrease, the ecliptic differs by twelve parts in twenty-four. At the nine limits the ecliptic differs by three degrees and the lunar path by three-fourths of a degree—all waxing and waning compensating each other. If the conjunction coincides with the two solstices, at the near initial limit of the green and white courses the ecliptic decreases by twelve parts in twenty-four and the lunar path increases by twelve parts in forty-eight. At the end of the half conjunction the ecliptic increases by twelve parts in twenty-four and the lunar path decreases by twelve parts in forty-eight. At the nine limits the ecliptic and lunar path differ equally—for retreat and hiding cancel each other out.
91
日出入赤道二十四度，月出入黃道六度，相距則四分之一，故於九道之變，以四立為中交。 在二分，增四分之一，而與黃道度相半。 在二至，減四分之一，而與黃道度正均。 故推極其數，引而伸之，每氣移一候。 月道所差，增損九分之一，七十二候而九道究矣。
The sun enters and exits the equator by twenty-four degrees; the moon enters and exits the ecliptic by six degrees—a ratio of one to four—so in the nine courses' changes the four Establishments serve as the middle conjunction. At the two equinoxes, add one-quarter, halving the ecliptic degrees. At the two solstices, subtract one-quarter, evenly matching the ecliptic degrees. Therefore, extending these numbers to the utmost and expanding them step by step, each qi shifts by one hou. The lunar path's deviation increases and decreases by one-ninth; in seventy-two hou the nine courses are complete.
92
凡月交一終，退前所交一度及餘八萬九千七百七十三分度之四萬二千五百三少半，積二百二十一月及分七千七百五十三，而交道周天矣。 因而半之，將九年而九道終。
Each time the moon completes one conjunction cycle, it retreats from the prior conjunction by one degree plus a remainder of 89,773 parts in 4°42,503 and a fraction over half; accumulated over 221 months and 7,753 parts, the conjunction path completes its circuit. Halving this, in about nine years the nine courses are complete.
93
以四象考之，各據合朔所交，入七十二候，則其八道之行也，以朔交為交初，望交為交中。 若交初在冬至初候而入陰曆，則行青道。 又十三日七十六分日之四十六，至交中得所衝之宿，變入陽曆，亦行青道。 若交初入陽曆，則白道也。 故考交初所入，而周天之度可知。 若望交在冬至初候，則減十三日四十六分，視大雪初候陰陽曆而正其行也。
Examining by the four quadrants, each based on the new-moon conjunction, entering seventy-two hou—the eight courses travel with initial conjunction at new moon and middle conjunction at full moon. If initial conjunction falls in the winter solstice initial hou and enters the yin calendar, the moon travels the green course. After thirteen days and forty-six ninety-sixths of a day, reaching middle conjunction at the opposing lodge, it shifts into the yang calendar and likewise travels the green course. If initial conjunction enters the yang calendar, it is the white course. Therefore, by examining what initial conjunction enters, the degrees of the full circuit can be known. If middle conjunction falls in the winter solstice initial hou, subtract thirteen days and forty-six parts and consult the Great Snow initial hou of the Yin-Yang calendar to correct its path.
94
其十晷漏中星略例曰：
Its tenth summary on gnomon shadows, clepsydra measures, and meridian stars says:
95
日行有南北，晷漏有長短。 然二十四氣晷差徐疾不同者，句股使然也。 直規中則差遲，與句股數齊則差急。 隨辰極高下，所遇不同，如黃道刻漏。 此乃數之淺者，近代且猶未曉。 今推黃道去極，與晷景、漏刻、昏距、中星四術返覆相求，消息同率，旋相為中，以合九服之變。
The sun's daily path varies north and south; gnomon shadows and clepsydra measures vary long and short. Yet the twenty-four qi gnomon deviations differ in slowness and speed—all because of the right triangle. At the perpendicular ruler's center the deviation is slow; when aligned with the right-triangle numbers it is fast. Following the celestial pole's height, what it encounters differs—like the ecliptic clepsydra divisions. This is elementary arithmetic—recent times have still not understood it. Now we derive the ecliptic's distance from the pole together with gnomon shadow, clepsydra measure, twilight distance, and meridian stars—the four methods seeking each other in reverse, waxing and waning at the same rate, rotating to find the center, to match changes across the nine domains.
96
其十一日蝕議曰：
Its eleventh discourse on solar eclipses says:
97
小雅「十月之交，朔日辛卯」。 虞𠠎以曆推之，在幽王六年。 開元曆定交分四萬三千四百二十九，入蝕限，加時在晝。 交會而蝕，數之常也。 詩云：「彼月而食，則維其常。 此日而食，于何不臧。 」日，君道也，無朏魄之變； 月，臣道也，遠日益明，近日益虧。 望與日軌相會，則徙而浸遠，遠極又徙而近交，所以著臣人之象也。 望而正於黃道，是謂臣干君明，則陽斯蝕之矣。 朔而正於黃道，是謂臣壅君明，則陽為之蝕矣。 且十月之交，於曆當蝕，君子猶以為變，詩人悼之。 然則古之太平，日不蝕，星不孛，蓋有之矣。
The Xiaoya says, "At the junction of the tenth month, on the first day xinmao." Yu Piao calculated by the calendar—it falls in the sixth year of King You. The Kaiyuan calendar fixes the conjunction fraction at 43,429, entering the eclipse limit; the hour falls in daylight. Conjunction meeting and eclipse—this is the regular pattern of numbers. The Odes say, "When the moon is eclipsed, that is its regular pattern. But when the sun is eclipsed, why is it not good? " The sun is the way of the lord—without waxing and waning changes; the moon is the way of the minister—farther from the sun it grows brighter, nearer it grows dimmer. When full moon and the sun's path meet, it shifts and recedes far; at the farthest it shifts again toward near conjunction—thus displaying the image of minister and subject. When full moon aligns with the ecliptic, this is called the minister confronting the lord's brightness—then the yang is eclipsed. When new moon aligns with the ecliptic, this is called the minister blocking the lord's brightness—then the yang is eclipsed by it. Moreover, the junction of the tenth month should eclipse by the calendar—yet the gentleman still regarded it as a portent, and the poet lamented it. Then in antiquity's age of great peace, the sun was not eclipsed and stars showed no comets—perhaps there were such times.
98
若過至未分，月或變行而避之； 或五星潛在日下，禦侮而救之； 或涉交數淺，或在陽曆，陽盛陰微則不蝕； 或德之休明，而有小眚焉，則天為之隱，雖交而不蝕。 此四者，皆德教之所由生也。
If the solstice had not yet divided, the moon might change course to avoid it; or the five planets might lurk beneath the sun, repelling the affront and saving it; or the conjunction fraction might be shallow, or it might be in the yang calendar—when yang is strong and yin weak, there is no eclipse; or virtue was magnificent and there was only a slight blemish—then heaven concealed it; though in conjunction, no eclipse occurred. These four all arise from virtue and teaching.
99
四序之中，分同道，至相過，交而有蝕，則天道之常。 如劉歆、賈逵，皆近古大儒，豈不知軌道所交，朔望同術哉？ 以日蝕非常，故闕而不論。
Among the four seasons, equinoxes share the same path and solstices pass each other—conjunction with eclipse is heaven's regular pattern. Men like Liu Xin and Jia Kui—both great Confucians near antiquity—how could they not know that path conjunction and new and full moon share the same method? Because solar eclipse was abnormal, they omitted it and did not discuss it.
100
黃初已來，治曆者始課日蝕疎密，及張子信而益詳。 劉焯、張冑玄之徒自負其術，謂日月皆可以密率求，是專於曆紀者也。
Since the Huangchu era, calendar-makers began assessing solar eclipse frequency; with Zhang Zixin it became more detailed. Liu Chuo, Zhang Zengxuan, and their ilk prided themselves on their methods, saying sun and moon could both be sought by dense ratios—they were devoted solely to calendar reckoning.
101
以戊寅、麟德曆推春秋日蝕，大最皆入蝕限。 於曆應蝕而春秋不書者尚多，則日蝕必在交限，其入限者不必盡蝕。 開元十二年七月戊午朔，於曆當蝕半強，自交趾至于朔方，候之不蝕。 十三年十二月庚戌朔，於曆當蝕太半，時東封泰山，還次梁、宋間，皇帝徹饍，不舉樂，不蓋，素服，日亦不蝕。 時羣臣與八荒君長之來助祭者，降物以需，不可勝數，皆奉壽稱慶，肅然神服。 雖算術乖舛，不宜如此，然後知德之動天，不俟終日矣。 若因開元二蝕，曲變交限而從之，則差者益多。
Using the Wuyin and Linde calendars to project Spring and Autumn solar eclipses, nearly all enter the eclipse limit. Where the calendar predicts eclipse but the Spring and Autumn Annals does not record it, many cases remain—therefore solar eclipse must fall within the conjunction limit, yet entering the limit does not necessarily mean eclipse. In the twelfth year of Kaiyuan, seventh month, wu day new moon—the calendar predicted more than half eclipse; from Jiaozhi to Shuofang, observers found no eclipse. Thirteenth year, twelfth month, geng day new moon—the calendar predicted more than three-quarters eclipse; at the time the emperor was returning from fengshan at Mount Tai, stopping between Liang and Song; the emperor withdrew provisions, ceased music, removed his canopy, wore plain robes—and the sun was not eclipsed. At the time assembled ministers and lordlings from the eight directions had come to assist the sacrifice, presenting gifts in wait beyond counting—all offered blessings for long life and praised the occasion, reverently awed. Though the arithmetic was wrong and should not have been so, one then knew that virtue moves heaven without waiting a full day. If one bent the conjunction limits to fit the two Kaiyuan non-eclipses, errors would increase all the more.
102
自開元治曆，史官每歲較節氣中晷，因檢加時小餘，雖大數有常，然亦與時推移，每歲不等。 晷變而長，則日行黃道南； 晷變而短，則日行黃道北。 行而南，則陰曆之交也或失； 行而北，則陽曆之交也或失。 日在黃道之中，且猶有變，況月行九道乎！ 杜預云：「日月動物，雖行度有大量，不能不小有盈縮。 故有雖交會而不蝕者，或有頻交而蝕者。 」是也。
Since Kaiyuan calendar reform, the historiographers each year compared midsummer gnomon at the qi, inspecting the hour's small remainder—though the great numbers are regular, they also shift with time, unequal each year. When the gnomon grows longer, the sun travels south on the ecliptic; when the gnomon grows shorter, the sun travels north on the ecliptic. Traveling south, the yin calendar's conjunction may err; traveling north, the yang calendar's conjunction may err. The sun in the midst of the ecliptic still has variation—how much more the moon traveling the nine courses! Du Yu said, "Sun and moon are moving bodies; though their degrees have great measures, they cannot but have small expansions and contractions. Therefore sometimes though in conjunction there is no eclipse, and sometimes there are frequent conjunctions with eclipse. " This is so.
103
故較曆必稽古史，虧蝕深淺、加時朓朒陰陽，其數相叶者，反覆相求，由曆數之中，以合辰象之變； 觀辰象之變，反求曆數之中。 類其所同，而中可知矣； 辨其所異，而變可知矣。 其循度則合于曆，失行則合于占。 占道順成，常執中以追變； 曆道逆數，常執中以俟變。 知此之說者，天道如視諸掌。
Therefore comparing calendars must consult ancient histories—eclipse depth, hour, waxing and waning, yin and yang; where the numbers agree, seek back and forth repeatedly, from within the calendar numbers to match celestial changes; observing celestial changes, seek back the calendar's midpoint. Classifying what is the same, the center can be known; distinguishing what differs, the variation can be known. Following the degrees, it agrees with the calendar; losing the path, it agrees with omen-reading. The omen path follows success, always holding the center to pursue change; the calendar path counts in reverse, always holding the center to await change. Who understands this saying knows heaven's way as if seen in the palm.
104
略例曰：舊曆考日蝕淺深，皆自張子信所傳，云積候所得，而未曉其然也。 以圓儀度日月之徑，乃以月徑之半減入交初限一度半，餘為闇虛半徑。 以月去黃道每度差數，令二徑相掩，以驗蝕分，以所入日遲疾乘徑，為泛所用刻數，大率去交不及三度，即月行沒在闇虛，皆入既限。 又半日月之徑，減春分入交初限相去度數，餘為斜射所差。 乃考差數，以立既限。 而優游進退於二度中間，亦令二徑相掩，以知日蝕分數。 月徑踰既限之南，則雖在陰曆，而所虧類同外道，斜望使然也。 既限之外，應向外蝕，外道交分，準用此例。 以較古今日蝕四十三事，月蝕九十九事，課皆第一。
The summary says: Old calendars assessing solar eclipse depth all derive from Zhang Zixin's transmission—accumulated hou observations obtained, yet without understanding why. Using the circular instrument to measure sun and moon diameters, then halving the moon's diameter and subtracting from the near initial conjunction limit of one and a half degrees, the remainder is the shadow cone's half-radius. Using the moon's degree-difference from the ecliptic, have the two diameters mutually mask to verify eclipse fraction; multiply diameter by the sun's slow-fast entry for the general clock number used; broadly, less than three degrees from conjunction means the moon's path is submerged in the shadow cone—all enter total eclipse limit. Also halving sun and moon diameters, subtract from the spring equinox initial conjunction limit's distance in degrees; the remainder is the oblique projection difference. Then examine the difference numbers to establish the total eclipse limit. And leisurely advancing and retreating within two degrees, likewise have the two diameters mutually mask to know solar eclipse fraction. When the moon's diameter exceeds south of the total limit, though in the yin calendar, the obscuration resembles the outer path—oblique viewing makes it so. Outside the total limit, it should eclipse outward; outer path conjunction fraction follows this precedent. Comparing forty-three ancient and modern solar eclipses and ninety-nine lunar eclipses, all assessments rank first.
105
使日蝕皆不可以常數求，則無以稽曆數之疎密。 若皆可以常數求，則無以知政教之休咎。 今更設考日蝕或限術，得常則合于數。 又日月交會大小相若，而月在日下，自京師斜射而望之，假中國食既，則南方戴日之下所虧纔半，月外反觀，則交而不蝕。 步九服日晷以定蝕分，晨昏漏刻與地偕變，則宇宙雖廣，可以一術齊之矣。
If solar eclipses could not all be sought by regular numbers, there would be no way to assess the calendar's density or looseness. If they could all be sought by regular numbers, there would be no way to know the blessings and calamities of government and teaching. Now we further establish a method for assessing solar eclipses or limits—when regular, it agrees with the numbers. Moreover, sun and moon conjunctions are roughly similar in size, and when the moon is beneath the sun, viewed obliquely from the capital, if China sees total eclipse, then south beneath the sun's disk only half is obscured; viewed from outside the moon's path, there is conjunction but no eclipse. Step the nine domains' solar gnomon shadows to fix eclipse fraction; dawn and dusk clepsydra measures change with the land—then though the cosmos is vast, one method can align it all.
106
其十二五星議曰：
Its twelfth discourse on the five planets says:
107
歲星自商、周迄春秋之季，率百二十餘年而超一次。 戰國後其行寖急，至漢尚微差，及哀、平間，餘勢乃盡，更八十四年而超一次，因以為常。 此其與餘星異也。 姬氏出自靈威仰之精，受木行正氣。 歲星主農祥，后稷憑焉，故周人常閱其禨祥，而觀善敗。 其始王也，次于鶉火，以達天黿。 及其衰也，淫于玄枵，以害鳥帑。 其後羣雄力爭，禮樂隕壞，而從衡攻守之術興。 故歲星常贏行於上，而侯王不寧於下，則木緯失行之勢，宜極於火運之中，理數然也。
From Shang and Zhou through the end of the Spring and Autumn period, Jupiter on average exceeded one cycle every hundred twenty-odd years. After the Warring States its motion gradually quickened; in Han there was still slight discrepancy; by the Ai and Ping reigns the remaining momentum was exhausted—it exceeded one cycle every eighty-four years, and this was taken as regular. This is how it differs from the other stars. The Ji clan issued from the essence of Lingweiyang, receiving the Wood phase's proper qi. Jupiter governs agricultural omens; Hou Ji relied on it—therefore the Zhou people constantly observed its portents and watched fortune and failure. At their first kingship, they halted at Quail Fire to reach Heaven's Turtle. At their decline, they strayed into Dark Ridge, harming the Bird's Nest. Afterward rival heroes contended fiercely, rites and music collapsed, and vertical-horizontal alliance and attack arts arose. Therefore Jupiter constantly advanced above while lords and kings were unsettled below—then the Wood planet's aberrant motion should reach its extreme within the Fire phase's course; such is the pattern of principle and number.
108
開元十二年正月庚午，歲星在進賢東北尺三寸，直軫十二度，於麟德曆在軫十五度。 推而上之，至漢河平二年，其十月下旬，歲星在軒轅南耑大星西北尺所。 麟德曆在張二度，直軒轅大星。 上下相距七百五十年，考其行度，猶未甚盈縮，則哀、平後不復每歲漸差也。 又上百二十年，至孝景中元三年五月，星在東井、鉞。 麟德曆在參三度。 又上六十年，得漢元年十月，五星聚于東井，從歲星也，於秦正歲在乙未，夏正當在甲午。 麟德曆白露八日，歲星留觜觿一度。 明年立夏，伏于參。 由差行未盡，而以常數求之使然也。 又上二百七十一年，至哀公十七年，歲在鶉火，麟德曆初見在輿鬼二度。 立冬九日，留星三度。 明年啟蟄十日退至柳五度，猶不及鶉火。 又上百七十八年，至僖公五年，歲星當在大火。 麟德曆初見在張八度，明年伏于翼十六度，定在鶉火，差三次矣。 哀公以後，差行漸遲，相去猶近； 哀公以前，率常行遲。 而舊曆猶用急率，不知合變，故所差彌多。 武王革命，歲星亦在大火，而麟德曆在東壁三度，則唐、虞已上，所差周天矣。
Kaiyuan twelfth year, first month, gengwu day—Jupiter was one chi three cun northeast of Jinxian, directly at twelve degrees of Chariot; on the Linde calendar it was at fifteen degrees of Chariot. Projecting upward to Han He Ping second year, in the latter ten days of the tenth month, Jupiter was about one chi northwest of the southern tip of the Great Star of Chariot. The Linde calendar placed it at two degrees of Net, directly at the Great Star of Chariot. Seven hundred fifty years apart above and below—examining its motion degrees, there was not yet much expansion or contraction; after Ai and Ping it no longer gradually differed each year. Another hundred twenty years upward—to Xiaojing Zhongyuan third year, fifth month, the star was at Well and Battle-Axe. The Linde calendar placed it at three degrees of Three Stars. Another sixty years upward—to Han first year, tenth month, the five planets gathered at Well, following Jupiter; by Qin reckoning the year was yiwei, by Xia reckoning it should be jiawu. The Linde calendar on White Dew eighth day had Jupiter stationary at one degree of Turtle Beak. The next year at Establishment of Summer it was hidden at Three Stars. Because differential motion had not finished, yet regular numbers were used to seek it—this made it so. Another two hundred seventy-one years upward—to Duke Ai seventeenth year, the year was at Quail Fire; the Linde calendar's first appearance was at two degrees of Ghost. Nine days after Establishment of Winter, the star was stationary three degrees. The next year ten days after Awakening of Insects it retreated to five degrees of Willow, still not reaching Quail Fire. Another hundred seventy-eight years upward—to Duke Xi fifth year, Jupiter should have been at Great Fire. The Linde calendar's first appearance was at eight degrees of Net; the next year it was hidden at sixteen degrees of Wings, fixed at Quail Fire—three cycles off. After Duke Ai, differential motion gradually slowed—the distance was still near; before Duke Ai, it generally moved slowly at regular speed. Yet old calendars still used the fast ratio, not knowing how to match change—therefore discrepancies grew ever more. At King Wu's revolution Jupiter was also at Great Fire, yet the Linde calendar placed it at three degrees of Eastern Wall—then from Tang and Yu upward, the discrepancy was a full circuit.
109
太初、三統曆歲星十二周天超一次，推商、周間事，大抵皆合。 驗開元注記，差九十餘度，蓋不知歲星後率故也。 皇極、麟德曆七周天超一次，以推漢、魏間事尚未差。 上驗春秋所載，亦差九十餘度，蓋不知歲星前率故也。 天保、天和曆得二率之中，故上合於春秋，下猶密於記注。 以推永平、黃初間事，遠者或差三十餘度，蓋不知戰國後歲星變行故也。 自漢元始四年，距開元十二年，凡十二甲子，上距隱公六年，亦十二甲子。 而二曆相合於其中，或差三次於古，或差三次於今，其兩合於古今者，中間亦乖。 欲一術以求之，則不可得也。
The Taichu and Triple Concordance calendars had Jupiter exceed one cycle every twelve circuits; projecting Shang and Zhou events, most all agreed. Checking Kaiyuan annotation records, the discrepancy was ninety-odd degrees—because they did not know Jupiter's later ratio. The Huangji and Linde calendars had it exceed one cycle every seven circuits; projecting Han and Wei events there was not yet discrepancy. Checking upward against Spring and Autumn records, the discrepancy was also ninety-odd degrees—because they did not know Jupiter's earlier ratio. The Tianbao and Tianhe calendars obtained the mean of the two ratios—therefore upward they agreed with Spring and Autumn, downward they were still denser than annotation records. Projecting Yongping and Huangchu events, the distant cases differed thirty-odd degrees—because they did not know Jupiter's changed motion after the Warring States. From Han Yuanshi fourth year to Kaiyuan twelfth year, twelve jiazi cycles in all; upward to Duke Yin sixth year, also twelve jiazi cycles. Yet the two calendars agreed at the midpoint—three cycles off from antiquity, or three cycles off from the present; where both agreed with antiquity and present, the middle still diverged. Wishing to seek it with one method—it cannot be obtained.
110
開元曆歲星前率，三百九十八日，餘二千二百一十九，秒九十三。 自哀公二十年丙寅後，每加度餘一分，盡四百三十九合，次合乃加秒十三而止，凡三百九十八日，餘二千六百五十九，秒六，而與日合，是為歲星後率。 自此因以為常，入漢元始六年也。
The Kaiyuan calendar's Jupiter earlier ratio: 398 days, remainder 2,219, 93 seconds. After Duke Ai twentieth year bingyin, each cycle adds one part to the degree remainder, through 439 conjunctions; at the next conjunction 13 seconds are added and stop—altogether 398 days, remainder 2,659, 6 seconds, then conjunction with the sun—this is Jupiter's later ratio. From this it was taken as regular—entering Han Yuanshi sixth year.
111
歲星差合術曰：置哀公二十年冬至合餘，加入差已來中積分，以前率約之，為入差合數。 不盡者如曆術入之，反求冬至後合日，乃副列入差合數，增下位一算，乘而半之，盈大衍通法為日，不盡為日餘，以加合日，即差合所在也。 求歲星差行徑術，以後終率約上元以來中積分，亦得所求。 若稽其實行，當從元始六年置差步之，則前後相距，間不容髮，而上元之首，無忽微空積矣。
The Jupiter differential conjunction method says: Set the winter solstice conjunction remainder of Duke Ai twentieth year, add the accumulated middle parts since entering differential motion, divide by the earlier ratio to obtain the entering differential conjunction number. What remains, enter by calendar method; seek back the day after winter solstice conjunction; then set the entering differential conjunction number as auxiliary entry, add one count to the lower place, multiply and halve; what fills the Dayan universal divisor becomes days, remainder becomes day remainder, add to conjunction day—this is where the differential conjunction lies. To seek the Jupiter differential motion diameter method, divide accumulated middle parts since upper origin by the later terminal ratio—this also obtains what is sought. If checking its actual motion, one should set differential steps from Yuanshi sixth year—then front and back distances allow no hair's breadth, and at upper origin's head there is no minute empty accumulation.
112
成湯伐桀，歲在壬戌，開元曆星與日合于角，次于氐十度而後退行。 其明年，湯始建國為元祀，順行與日合于房，所以紀商人之命也。
When Cheng Tang attacked Jie, the year was renxu; the Kaiyuan calendar has the star in conjunction with the sun at Horn, halting at ten degrees of Base then retreating. The next year Tang first established the state as the inaugural reign; direct motion and sun conjunction at Room—thus recording the Shang people's mandate.
113
後六百一算至紂六祀，周文王初禴于畢，十三祀歲在己卯，星在鶉火，武王嗣位。 克商之年，進及輿鬼，而退守東井。 明年，周始革命，順行與日合于柳，進留于張。 考其分野，則分陝之間，與三監封域之際也。
After 601 cycles to Zhou sixth year of Zhou, King Wen first performed spring sacrifice at Bi; thirteenth year the year was jimao, star at Quail Fire, King Wu succeeded. The year he overcame Shang, it advanced to Chariot and Ghost, then retreated to guard Eastern Well. The next year Zhou first revolutionized; direct motion and sun conjunction at Willow, advancing to station at Net. Examining its territorial allotment, it was between the partition of Shaan and the borders of the Three Overseers' fiefs.
114
成王三年，歲在丙午，星在大火，唐叔始封，故國語曰：「晉之始封，歲在大火。 」春秋傳僖公五年，歲在大火，晉公子重耳自蒲奔狄。 十六年，歲在壽星，適齊過衞，野人與之塊，子犯曰：「天賜也，天事必象，歲及鶉火必有此乎！ 復于壽星，必獲諸侯。 」二十三年，歲星在胃、昴。 秦伯納晉文公。 董因曰：「歲在大梁，將集天行。 元年，實沈之星，晉人是居。 君之行也，歲在大火，閼伯之星也，是謂大辰。 辰以善成，后稷是相，唐叔以封。 且以辰出而以參入，皆晉祥也。 」二十七年，歲在鶉火，晉侯伐衞，取五鹿，敗楚師于城濮，始獲諸侯。 歲適及壽星，皆與開元曆合。
King Cheng third year, year at bingwu, star at Great Fire, Tang Shu first enfeoffed—therefore the Discourses of the States says, "When Jin was first enfeoffed, the year was at Great Fire." The Spring and Autumn Annals, Duke Xi fifth year, year at Great Fire—Duke Wen of Jin fled from Pu to Di. Sixteenth year, year at Longevity Star, going to Qi passing Wei, rustics gave him a clod; Zi Fan said, "Heaven's gift! Heaven's affairs must have images—when the year reaches Quail Fire there must be this!" Returning to Longevity Star, he must obtain the feudal lords. Twenty-third year, Jupiter at Stomach and Hairy Head. Duke Mu of Qin received Duke Wen of Jin. Dong Yin said, "The year at Great Bridge, about to gather Heaven's motion. First year, the stars of Real Shen—Jin people dwell there. My lord's journey—the year at Great Fire, Yan Bo's star, this is called Great Chen. Chen completes through goodness; Hou Ji was its minister; Tang Shu was enfeoffed thereby. Moreover exiting by Chen and entering by Three Stars—all Jin's auspices." Twenty-seventh year, year at Quail Fire—Duke of Jin attacked Wei, took Wulu, defeated Chu army at Chengpu, first obtained feudal lords. The year reaching Longevity Star—all agree with the Kaiyuan calendar.
115
襄公十八年，歲星在陬訾之口，開元曆大寒三日，星與日合，在危三度，遂順行至營室八度。 其明年，鄭子蟜卒。 將葬，公孫子羽與裨竈晨會事焉，過伯有氏，其門上生莠，子羽曰：「其莠猶在乎，於是歲在降婁中而曙。 」裨竈指之曰：「猶可以終歲，歲不及此次也。 」開元曆，歲星在奎。 奎，降婁也。 麟德曆，在危。 危，玄枵也。 二十八年春，無冰。 梓慎曰：「歲在星紀，而淫於玄枵。 」裨竈曰：「歲棄其次，而旅於明年之次，以害鳥帑。 周、楚惡之。 」開元曆，歲星至南斗十七度，而退守西建間，復順行，與日合于牛初。 應在星紀，而盈行進及虛宿，故曰「淫」。 留玄枵二年，至三十年。 開元曆，歲星順行至營室十度，留。 距子蟜之卒一終矣。 其年八月，鄭人殺良霄，故曰「及其亡也，歲在陬訾之口」。 其明年，乃及降婁。
Duke Xiang eighteenth year, Jupiter at the mouth of Zouzi; Kaiyuan calendar Great Cold third day, star and sun in conjunction at three degrees of Rooftop, then direct motion to eight degrees of Encampment. The next year Zichan of Zheng died. About to bury him, Gongsun Ziyu and Pi Zao met early for the funeral affairs; passing Bo You's house, weeds grew on its gate; Ziyu said, "The weeds are still there—at this time the year was in Descending Harvest's middle and dawn." Pi Zao pointed and said, "Still can finish the year—the year will not reach this time." Kaiyuan calendar: Jupiter at Legs. Legs—Descending Harvest. Linde calendar: at Rooftop. Rooftop—Dark Ridge. Twenty-eighth year spring, no ice. Zishen said, "The year at Star Record, yet straying into Dark Ridge." Pi Zao said, "The year abandons its place, traveling to next year's place, harming the Bird's Nest." Zhou and Chu hated it. Kaiyuan calendar: Jupiter reached seventeen degrees of Southern Dipper, then retreated to guard between Western Establishment, again direct motion, sun conjunction at Ox beginning. It should be at Star Record, yet advancing motion reached and passed Void lodge—therefore called "straying." Stationary at Dark Ridge two years, until thirtieth year. Kaiyuan calendar: Jupiter direct motion to ten degrees of Encampment, stationary. One full cycle from Zichan's death. That year eighth month, Zheng people killed Liang Xiao—therefore "at his death the year was at the mouth of Zouzi." The next year it reached Descending Harvest.
116
昭公八年十一月，楚滅陳。 史趙曰：「未也。 陳，顓頊之族也。 歲在鶉火，是以卒滅。 今在析木之津，猶將復由。 」開元曆，在箕八度，析木津也。 十年春，進及婺女初，在玄枵之維首。 傳曰：「正月，有星出于婺女。 」裨竈曰：「今茲歲在顓頊之墟。 」是歲與日合于危。 其明年進及營室，復得豕韋之次。 景王問萇弘曰：「今茲諸侯何實吉？ 何實凶？ 」對曰：「蔡凶。 此蔡侯般殺其君之歲，歲在豕韋，弗過此矣，楚將有之。 歲及大梁，蔡復楚凶。 」至十三年，歲星在昴、畢，而楚弒靈王，陳、蔡復封。 初，昭公九年，陳災。 裨竈曰：「後五年，陳將復封。 歲五及鶉火，而後陳卒亡。 」自陳災五年，而歲在大梁，陳復建國。 哀公十七年，五及鶉火，而楚滅陳。 是年，歲星與日合在張六度。 昭公三十一年夏，吳伐越。 始用師於越也，史墨曰：「越得歲而吳伐之，必受其凶。 」是歲，星與日合于南斗三度。 昔僖公六年，歲陰在卯，星在析木。 昭公三十二年，亦歲陰在卯，而星在星紀。 故三統曆因以為超次之率。 考其實，猶百二十餘年。 近代諸曆，欲以八十四年齊之，此其所惑也。 後三十八年而越滅吳，星三及斗、牛，已入差合二年矣。
Duke Zhao eighth year eleventh month, Chu destroyed Chen. Shi Zhao said, "Not yet." Chen is Zhuan Xu's clan. The year at Quail Fire—therefore it finally perished. Now at the ford of Split Wood, it will still return thereby. Kaiyuan calendar: at eight degrees of Winnowing Basket—Split Wood ford. Tenth year spring, advancing to Maiden beginning, at Dark Ridge's corner head. The Annals says, "First month, a star appeared at Maiden." Pi Zao said, "This year at Zhuan Xu's mound." That year in conjunction with the sun at Rooftop. The next year advancing to Encampment, again obtaining Pig Wei's place. King Jing asked Chang Hong, "This year which feudal lords are truly auspicious? Which truly inauspicious?" He replied, "Cai is inauspicious. This is the year Marquis Ban of Cai killed his lord—the year at Pig Wei—it will not pass this; Chu will possess it. When the year reaches Great Bridge, Cai again and Chu inauspicious." By the thirteenth year, Jupiter at Hairy Head and Net; Chu assassinated King Ling, Chen and Cai were re-enfeoffed. Initially, Duke Zhao ninth year, Chen suffered fire. Pi Zao said, "After five years, Chen will be re-enfeoffed. Five times reaching Quail Fire, then Chen finally perishes." Five years from Chen's fire, the year at Great Bridge, Chen re-established the state. Duke Ai seventeenth year, five times reaching Quail Fire, Chu destroyed Chen. That year, Jupiter and sun in conjunction at six degrees of Net. Duke Zhao thirty-first year summer, Wu attacked Yue. When first deploying troops against Yue, Shi Mo said, "Yue obtains the year yet Wu attacks—it must receive calamity." That year, star and sun in conjunction at three degrees of Southern Dipper. Formerly Duke Xi sixth year, year yin at mao, star at Split Wood. Duke Zhao thirty-second year, also year yin at mao, yet star at Star Record. Therefore the Triple Concordance calendar took this as the exceeding-cycle rate. Checking the reality, it was still hundred twenty-odd years. Recent calendars wished to align it with eighty-four years—this is where they were confused. Thirty-eight years later Yue destroyed Wu—the star three times reached Dipper and Ox, already two years into differential conjunction.
117
夫五事感於中，而五行之祥應于下，五緯之變彰于上。 若聲發而響和，形動而影隨，故王者失典刑之正，則星辰為之亂行； 汨彝倫之敍，則天事為之無象。 當其亂行、無象，又可以曆紀齊乎？ 故襄公二十八年，歲在星紀，淫于玄枵。 至三十年八月，始及陬訾之口，超次而前，二年守之。
The five affairs are stirred within, and the five phases' omens respond below; the five planets' changes are manifest above. Like sound issuing and echo answering, form moving and shadow following—therefore when the king loses correct law and punishment, the stars and planets are disordered in motion for him; when human relations are disrupted, heaven's affairs lose their images. When they are disordered in motion and lose images, can one align them with calendar reckoning? Therefore Duke Xiang twenty-eighth year, year at Star Record, straying into Dark Ridge. By thirtieth year eighth month, first reaching the mouth of Zouzi, exceeding cycle and advancing, two years guarding it.
118
漢元鼎中，太白入于天苑，失行，在黃道南三十餘度。 間歲，武帝北巡守，登單于臺，勒兵十八萬騎，及誅大宛，馬大死軍中。
Mid Yuanding of Han, Venus entered Celestial Meadows, aberrant motion, thirty-odd degrees south of the ecliptic. The next year Emperor Wu toured north, ascended Chanyu Platform, mustered 180,000 cavalry, and when punishing Dayuan, horses died in great numbers in the army.
119
晉咸寧四年九月，太白當見不見，占曰：「是謂失舍，不有破軍，必有亡國。 」時將伐吳，明年三月，兵出，太白始夕見西方，而吳亡。
Xianning fourth year ninth month, Venus should appear but did not; the omen reads, "This is called losing lodging—if not broken armies, then ruined states." At the time about to attack Wu; next year third month, troops deployed; Venus first appeared at dusk in the west—and Wu perished.
120
永寧元年，正月至閏月，五星經天，縱橫無常。 永興二年四月丙子，太白犯狼星，失行，在黃道南四十餘度。 永嘉三年正月庚子，熒惑犯紫微。 皆天變所未有也，終以二帝蒙塵，天下大亂。
Yongning first year, first month through intercalary month, five planets crossed heaven, traversing without regularity. Yongxing second year fourth month bingzi, Venus violated Wolf Star, aberrant motion, forty-odd degrees south of the ecliptic. Yongjia third year first month gengzi, Mars violated Purple Palace. All were celestial changes never before seen—ending with two emperors suffering disgrace, great disorder under heaven.
121
後魏神瑞二年十二月，熒惑在瓠瓜星中，一夕忽亡，不知所在。 崔浩以日辰推之，曰：「庚午之夕，辛未之朝，天有陰雲，熒惑之亡，在此二日。 庚午未皆主秦，辛為西夷。 今姚興據咸陽，是熒惑入秦矣。 」其後熒惑果出東井，留守盤旋，秦中大旱赤地，昆明水竭。 明年，姚興死，二子交兵。 三年，國滅。
Later Wei Shenrui second year twelfth month, Mars in Bottle-Gourd stars, one night suddenly vanished, unknown where. Cui Hao calculated by day and time, "Gengwu evening, xinwei morning—heaven has cloudy cover; Mars's vanishing falls within these two days. Gengwu and wei both govern Qin; xin is western barbarians. Now Yao Xing holds Xianyang—Mars enters Qin." Afterward Mars indeed emerged from Eastern Well, stationary circling; great drought reddened the land in Qin, Kunming water dried up. The next year Yao Xing died, two sons fought each other. Third year, the state perished.
122
齊永明九年八月十四日，火星應退在昴三度，先歷在畢； 二十一日始逆行，北轉，垂及立冬，形色彌盛。 魏永平四年八月癸未，熒惑在氐，夕伏西方，亦先期五十餘日，雖時曆疎闊，不宜若此。
Qi Yongming ninth year eighth month fourteenth day, Mars should retreat at three degrees of Hairy Head, first passing at Net; twenty-first day first retrograde, turning north, extending to Establishment of Winter, color and form ever brighter. Wei Yongping fourth year eighth month guiwei, Mars at Base, hidden at dusk in the west, also fifty-odd days early—though calendars were loose, it should not be like this.
123
隋大業九年五月丁丑，熒惑逆行入南斗，色赤如血，大如三斗器，光芒震耀，長七八尺，於斗中句巳而行，亦天變所未有也。 後楊玄感反，天下大亂。
